notes: Batch G (ferrous sulfate, calcium carbonate, magnesium glycerophosphate, potassium chloride). BNF/BNFC not accessed (geo-blocked). FERROUS SULFATE: three UK SmPCs used (Wockhardt emc-3130, Sun/Ranbaxy emc-2623, Sandoz emc-4231) and they disagree: (a) children - Wockhardt and Sun say 'not recommended' for children; Sandoz gives weight-banded dosing for 6-12 years and says not recommended under 6 years or under 22 kg; (b) Sun lists regional enteritis/ulcerative colitis and paroxysmal nocturnal haemoglobinuria as contraindications, Wockhardt only cautions in IBD; (c) haemolytic anaemia is a contraindication in Wockhardt/Sun but a caution in Sandoz; (d) pregnancy - Wockhardt/Sun: avoid first trimester if possible unless (definite) evidence of iron deficiency, Sandoz: recommended in pregnancy and lactation. Separation intervals also differ between SmPCs: iron SmPCs say at least 2 hours from levothyroxine, quinolones and calcium/magnesium products; Eltroxin SmPC says 4-5 hours for levothyroxine vs antacids/calcium salts/oral iron; Adcal says allow a minimum of 4 hours before taking calcium after thyroxine/quinolones/iron; ciprofloxacin SmPC says take ciprofloxacin 1-2 hours before or at least 4 hours after multivalent cation products; Neomag says magnesium 3 to 4 hours before or after iron/aminoquinolines. Each kept as a separate rule with its own source. Separation-interval rules use level 'caution' with effect 'reduced-absorption'. CALCIUM CARBONATE: calcium-only product chosen (Adcal 1500mg chewable, 600 mg elemental calcium, no colecalciferol). Adcal-D3 and Calcichew-D3 type products (with colecalciferol) are NOT covered by this file. Calcichew 500 mg SmPC was not found on emc search. Adcal 1500 lists only rare mild GI effects (no common/very common effects). Calcium carbonate is listed in the 'antacid' group on the basis of Adcal 5.1 wording ('also widely used as an antacid'), so antacid interaction rules from other SmPCs (e.g. ciprofloxacin, hydroxychloroquine) will fire for it. Thiazide diuretics and digitalis interactions are in the section text only (no master-list member). MAGNESIUM GLYCEROPHOSPHATE: Neomag 4mmol chewable tablets (97.2 mg Mg per tablet). SmPC contraindicates GFR < 30 ml/min; SPS hypomagnesaemia page instead says seek specialist advice in CKD 4 or 5, AKI, dialysis or transplant and no oral dose adjustment in CKD 1 to 3 - both recorded. Neomag 4.5 does not mention levothyroxine or quinolones; the ciprofloxacin rule comes from the ciprofloxacin SmPC (magnesium named). Neomag names 'aminoquinolines' (hydroxychloroquine class per its SmPC 5.1) for a 3-4 hour separation. POTASSIUM CHLORIDE: two formulations - Sando-K effervescent tablets (emc-959; 12 mmol K+ per tablet stated by SPS; SmPC states 2 to 4 tablets = 24 to 48 mmol K+) and Kay-Cee-L 7.5% syrup (1 mmol K+ per mL; SmPC PDF from MHRA Products site, PL 39307/0145). Kay-Cee-L paediatric dose is in mL/kg, so no calc block was added (calc supports mg/kg only). Modified-release KCl tablets (8 mmol, per SPS) were not given a formulation: no UK SmPC found on emc. Trimethoprim SmPC (emc-4566) names potassium supplements (monitor potassium); co-trimoxazole SmPC (emc-6997, checked) does not name potassium supplements specifically, so no co-trimoxazole rule. Lisinopril SmPC: combination with potassium supplements 'not recommended' (avoid). Aldactone: potassium supplements 'should not be given routinely' (avoid). Not found in accessed UK sources: SPS breastfeeding pages for oral iron, magnesium glycerophosphate or potassium chloride; SPS monitoring pages for any of the four; BUMPS/UKTIS leaflets for iron, calcium, magnesium or potassium supplements (UKTIS has only an 'Iron overdose' monograph, not used); relevant MHRA Drug Safety Updates. Group memberships added for lisinopril (ace-inhibitor), spironolactone (potassium-sparing-diuretic), ciprofloxacin (fluoroquinolone) and hydroxychloroquine (antimalarial) from their own UK SmPCs; other batches may also define these. AUDIT 2026-10-17 (independent second check, see audit/G.md): antacid membership of calcium carbonate kept (Adcal 5.1 calls it an antacid; the antacid rules of ciprofloxacin, levothyroxine, hydroxychloroquine and naproxen were read: ciprofloxacin names calcium-containing antacids, Eltroxin names antacids and calcium salts, hydroxychloroquine and naproxen say only 'antacids'); added rules for the hereditary-fructose-intolerance condition (defined in batch E) alongside hereditary-sugar-intolerance; Neomag PKU/hyperphosphataemia raised to contraindicated (they sit in SmPC 4.3); Kay-Cee-L advanced severe renal failure added on the severe-renal-impairment condition (batch A); potassium + co-trimoxazole and Sando-K (bicarbonate) + iron rules added. The co-trimoxazole rule rests on the co-trimoxazole SmPC (emc-6999) caution with 'any other drugs that can cause hyperkalaemia' plus the Kay-Cee-L caution with medicines that raise plasma potassium; it supersedes the earlier 'no co-trimoxazole rule' note.
